acubi-style.Name: Acubi Style
acubi-style.Description: Minimalist, subversive Korean Y2K focusing on thin layers and neutral tones.
acubi-style.Notes: WARNING: Acubi is a minimalist, subversive take on Y2K focused on layering thin, neutral/dark fabrics. Less flashy than Cyber Y2K.

mcbling.Name: McBling
mcbling.Description: Tabloid celebrity era defined by loud logos, rhinestones, velour tracksuits, and hot pink.
mcbling.Notes: WARNING: Distinct from Cyber Y2K. McBling requires rhinestones, visible branding, and a trashy-chic 2000s tabloid vibe.

trad-goth.Name: Trad Goth
trad-goth.Description: The original post-punk goth look from UK clubs: black lace, fishnet, velvet and pointed boots, largely DIY.
trad-goth.Notes: WARNING: Trad Goth is the original 1980s post-punk look built on DIY, lace, fishnet and winklepickers. Do not confuse with Mall Goth (Hot Topic and nu-metal, 1999-2006), with Cybergoth (neon and PVC) or with Health Goth (monochrome sportswear).

post-punk-revival.Name: Post-Punk Revival
post-punk-revival.Description: Razor-sharp, gaunt rockstar tailoring heavily defined by Hedi Slimane's era at Dior Homme.
post-punk-revival.Notes: WARNING: Requires extremely sharp Parisian tailoring and a gaunt silhouette, distinct from casual grunge.

fairy-grunge.Name: Fairy Grunge
fairy-grunge.Description: Blends 90s Seattle grunge distressing with ethereal, earthy, and mystical nature elements.
IconicItems: Layered slip dresses over long sleeves
fairy-grunge.Notes: WARNING: Requires earthy, muted tones mixed with extreme distressing. Do not confuse with clean fairycore.

mod.Name: Mod
mod.Description: Sharp, slim British youth tailoring worn with parkas and scooters.
mod.Notes: WARNING: Mod is sharp, slim 1960s British tailoring with parkas and scooters. Do not confuse with Ivy Style (American, looser cut), with Britpop (the 1990s look that quotes it) or with Terrace Casuals.

cyber-y2k.Name: Cyber Y2K
cyber-y2k.Description: Futuristic, metallic aesthetics blending early internet optimism with rave culture.
cyber-y2k.Notes: WARNING: Cyber Y2K must include futuristic, metallic, or raver elements from the late 90s/early 00s. Do not confuse with McBling.

blokecore.Name: Blokecore
blokecore.Description: Modern revival of British pub and football casuals culture with vintage jerseys.
blokecore.Notes: WARNING: Blokecore strictly requires the contrast of vintage football jerseys with regular/straight denim and terrace sneakers. Do not classify full tracksuits here.

amekaji.Name: Amekaji
amekaji.Description: Japanese reproduction of mid-century American casual and military clothing, made by Japanese mills and brands.
amekaji.Notes: WARNING: Amekaji is American casual as rebuilt in Japan, with Japanese mills, brands and obsessive reproduction detail. Do not confuse with Heritage Workwear (original American makers), with City Boy (oversized prep) or with Ura-Hara (graphic streetwear).

opium.Name: Opium
opium.Description: Dark, avant-garde streetwear characterized by distorted silhouettes and heavy leather.
opium.Notes: WARNING: Opium is highly monochromatic (mostly black) with distorted, avant-garde streetwear silhouettes. Do not categorize standard traditional goth as Opium.

lolita.Name: Lolita
lolita.Description: Modest Japanese street fashion defined by a bell-shaped silhouette, petticoats and coordinated accessories.
lolita.Notes: WARNING: Lolita is a modest Japanese street fashion with a bell-shaped silhouette, unrelated to the novel of the same name. Do not confuse with Coquette, with costume or cosplay, or with Gyaru. Sweet, Gothic and Classic are distinct substyles.

ura-hara-harajuku-90s.Name: Ura-Hara (Harajuku 90s)
ura-hara-harajuku-90s.Description: Pioneering Tokyo streetwear blending punk, hip-hop, and DIY aesthetics.
ura-hara-harajuku-90s.Notes: WARNING: Ura-Hara is strictly late 90s/early 00s Tokyo streetwear rooted in punk and hip-hop. Do not confuse with modern generic streetwear.

indie-sleaze.Name: Indie Sleaze
indie-sleaze.Description: Messy, nocturnal bloghouse aesthetic mixing vintage thrifting with American Apparel basics.
indie-sleaze.Notes: WARNING: Indie Sleaze must look heavily partied-in and messy, distinct from clean modern indie.

twee.Name: Twee
twee.Description: Cute, vintage-inspired look of collars, cardigans and colored tights.
twee.Notes: WARNING: Twee is the cute, vintage-inspired 2008-2014 look of collars, cardigans and colored tights. Do not confuse with Indie Sleaze (same years, messy and nocturnal), with Coquette (bows and lace, more sensual) or with Cottagecore.

health-goth.Name: Health Goth
health-goth.Description: Monochromatic, dystopian athletic darkwear born on Tumblr, blending sportswear with industrial themes.
health-goth.Notes: WARNING: Distinct from Techwear. Health Goth is strictly sports/gym apparel styled in a sterile, dystopian all-black context.

ivy-style.Name: Ivy Style
ivy-style.Description: Natural-shoulder American campus dress of the postwar Ivy League.
ivy-style.Notes: WARNING: Ivy Style is the natural-shoulder American campus look of the 1950s and 60s. Do not confuse with City Boy (its oversized Japanese reinterpretation), with Old Money (a 2021+ social media look) or with Dark Academia.

goth-ninja.Name: Goth Ninja
goth-ninja.Description: Internet-born aesthetic mixing dark drapery, drop-crotch proportions, and artisanal boots.
goth-ninja.Notes: WARNING: Goth Ninja is specifically the 2009-2014 internet forum aesthetic characterized by extreme layering of thin, dark fabrics. Distinguish from modern Techwear.

y2k.Name: Y2K
y2k.Description: Umbrella term for 1995-2005 mainstream fashion, spanning the futuristic late-90s look and the logo-heavy, velour-and-rhinestone early-2000s look. Revived today as millennial nostalgia.
y2k.Notes:
WARNING: Y2K is the broad umbrella for 1995-2005 fashion. For precision use the two narrower entries: Cyber Y2K (futuristic, metallic, rave, late 90s) and McBling (rhinestones, velour, loud logos, 2003-2008). Do not treat them as interchangeable.

PRICE BREAKDOWN (verified Oct 2026):
- Velour tracksuit (Juicy Couture): $80-200 (Grailed, eBay)
- Low-rise jeans (vintage Tommy, GAP): $30-80 (Grailed, thrift)
- Sean John / Von Dutch: $40-120 (Grailed)
- Deadstock / Blumarine revival: $200-500+ (Grailed, eBay)
- Baby tee / butterfly clip: $10-30 (Depop, eBay)

WHERE TO BUY DETAILS:
- Depop: best for affordable Y2K and butterfly clips, $10-30
- Grailed: best for curated vintage Y2K, prices $50-200
- Thrift: cheapest but inconsistent
- eBay: deadstock and rare pieces, but watch for fakes

quiet-luxury.Name: Quiet Luxury
quiet-luxury.Description: Stealth wealth aesthetics focusing heavily on ultra-premium materials, perfect tailoring, and zero visible logos.
quiet-luxury.Notes: WARNING: Quiet luxury must have absolutely no visible logos or flashy details. Material quality is the only indicator.

hypebeast-streetwear.Name: Hypebeast Streetwear
hypebeast-streetwear.Description: Logo-driven streetwear built around limited drops, collaborations and resale value.
hypebeast-streetwear.Notes: WARNING: Hypebeast Streetwear is logo-driven, drop-based and resale-priced (2014-2019). Do not confuse with Ura-Hara (its 1990s Tokyo roots), with Skate (functional skate brands) or with Archive Fashion (historic runway pieces).

terrace-casuals.Name: Terrace Casuals
terrace-casuals.Description: British football-terrace look built on European designer sportswear and rare trainers.
terrace-casuals.Notes: WARNING: Terrace Casuals is designer sportswear worn on British football terraces, with no team colors or replica shirts. Do not confuse with Blokecore (2022+, vintage football jerseys), with Mod or with UK Roadman.

decora.Name: Decora
decora.Description: Harajuku style built on extreme layering of colorful accessories over bright, playful clothing.
IconicItems: Mismatched colorful socks and leg warmers
decora.Notes: WARNING: Decora is defined by extreme layering of colorful accessories, especially dozens of hair clips. Do not confuse with Lolita (structured, modest silhouette), with Gyaru or with generic kawaii outfits that lack the accessory layering.

mall-goth.Name: Mall Goth
mall-goth.Description: Nu-metal inspired mall rat aesthetic heavily commercialized by early 2000s Hot Topic.
mall-goth.Notes: WARNING: Mall Goth is specifically the Hot Topic/Nu-Metal commercial era, not traditional 80s trad goth.

subversive-basics.Name: Subversive Basics
subversive-basics.Description: Deconstructed wardrobe staples utilizing cut-outs, sheer layers, and asymmetric strapping.
subversive-basics.Notes: WARNING: Subversive basics look like traditional wardrobe staples that have been slashed, twisted, or reassembled. Focus on negative space.

frutiger-aero-fashion.Name: Frutiger Aero Fashion
frutiger-aero-fashion.Description: Tech-optimistic aesthetic defined by glossy textures, translucent fabrics, and aquatic colors.
frutiger-aero-fashion.Notes: WARNING: Frutiger Aero is an aesthetic of 2004-2013 tech-optimism. Clothing must feature glossy, translucent, or water-like textures (aqua, white). Not dystopian.

uk-roadman.Name: UK Roadman
uk-roadman.Description: British grime and drill uniform of matching tracksuits, Air Max trainers and crossbody bags.
IconicItems: Nike Air Max 95 and TN trainers
uk-roadman.Notes: WARNING: UK Roadman style is the grime and drill uniform of matching tracksuits and Air Max trainers. Do not confuse with Blokecore (football jerseys), with Terrace Casuals (1980s designer sportswear) or with Techwear, despite the shared Nike Tech Fleece.

whimsigoth.Name: Whimsigoth
whimsigoth.Description: Celestial, mystical 90s aesthetic blending bohemian silhouettes with dark romantic gothic elements.
whimsigoth.Notes: WARNING: Whimsigoth requires 90s celestial/witchy motifs and velvet, distinct from standard bohemian.

heritage-workwear.Name: Heritage Workwear
heritage-workwear.Description: American work clothing worn for its construction, durability and patina.
heritage-workwear.Notes: WARNING: Heritage Workwear is durable American work clothing from original makers, worn for construction and patina. Do not confuse with Amekaji (the Japanese reproduction scene), with Gorpcore (technical outdoor gear) or with Western Core.

gyaru.Name: Gyaru
gyaru.Description: Glamorous Shibuya youth style of tanned skin, bleached hair and bold, body-conscious outfits.
gyaru.Notes: WARNING: Gyaru is the glamorous Shibuya 109 look of tans, bleached hair and bold outfits. Do not confuse with Lolita (modest, doll-like, Harajuku) or with Decora. Its substyles (Kogal, Ganguro, Hime Gyaru) differ sharply from one another.

techwear.Name: Techwear
techwear.Description: Utilitarian, dystopian, and highly functional aesthetic focusing on advanced fabrics (like Gore-Tex), mobility, and weather resistance. It blends cyberpunk aesthetics with modern tactical and outdoor gear.
techwear.Notes:
WARNING: Techwear requires technical, weatherproof fabrics and a tactical, mostly black urban look. Do not confuse with Gorpcore (nature-oriented, earth tones) or with Goth Ninja (draped, non-technical fabrics).

PRICE BREAKDOWN (verified Oct 2026):
- Entry-level techwear (Nike ACG, Riot Division): $100-250 (Retail, Grailed)
- Mid-tier shells & cargos (Y-3, Stone Island Shadow Project): $300-600 (Retail, SSENSE)
- High-end/Grail pieces (ACRONYM jackets): $1000-2000+ (Grailed, Retail)
- Waterproof tech sneakers (Nike ACG, Salomon S/Lab): $150-250 (Retail)

WHERE TO BUY DETAILS:
- Grailed: The absolute best marketplace for secondhand and rare techwear (especially ACRONYM).
- SSENSE / END. Clothing: Best for buying new mid-to-high-end techwear brands.
- Official Sites: Essential for drops, as hype pieces sell out instantly.

CROSSOVERS:
- Heavily overlaps with Gorpcore (outdoor functionality) and Darkwear/Cyberpunk (aesthetic).

WHY IT'S RELEVANT:
- Driven by the gamification of fashion and a growing desire for clothing that acts as "gear" for surviving modern urban environments.

old-money.Name: Old Money
old-money.Description: Social media aesthetic imitating inherited wealth through preppy heritage staples.
old-money.Notes: WARNING: Old Money is an accessible social media look built on preppy signals such as cable knits, tennis whites and visible heritage logos. Do not confuse with Quiet Luxury (logo-free and priced far higher) or with Ivy Style (the 1950s-60s original).

emo.Name: Emo
emo.Description: Band-driven mid-2000s look in black and red: skinny jeans, band tees and studded belts.
emo.Notes: WARNING: Emo is the dark, band-driven 2002-2009 look in black and red. Do not confuse with Scene (neon, layered and louder), with Mall Goth (nu-metal, wide strap pants) or with E-girl / E-boy, the 2018+ online revival.

city-boy.Name: City Boy
city-boy.Description: Japanese interpretation of American traditional prep with highly oversized, relaxed, and slouchy silhouettes.
city-boy.Notes: WARNING: City Boy is specifically the Japanese 'Popeye Magazine' oversized prep, not slim-fit Ivy League.
